title: The Federal Reserve

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: You can't really run like a sophisticated capitalist economy without having some kind of central bank to

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: the currency. Okay. So we created the Federal Reserve in 1913 so we could have a national currency. The thing you and I call the dollar is a Federal Reserve note. Okay. So this bank, its basic primary job

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: to issue dollars and to issue them in a way. that we have a stable currency so that

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: the money supply gets tight, the Fed creates more dollars out of thin air and increases the money supply. And then when there's too much money out there, which creates inflation, the Fed like sucks in the money, like kind of draining a pool, brings money out, cools it down. And that's the job of the Federal Reserve, in essence, at the most basic level.
